case.dek: The dispute centers on whether a judge's instruction to ignore a co-defendant's confession satisfies the Sixth Amendment when that confession explicitly names the defendant.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Samia argues that a co-defendant's confession violates his rights even if the jury ignores it. The government argues that a proper jury instruction cures any constitutional defect.

The government argues that a jury instruction to ignore the evidence resolves the issue.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of jury instructions in criminal trials. It determines whether specific evidence can be admitted despite constitutional concerns. The outcome shapes how courts handle co-defendant confessions.
